text: Your price tag never moved, but you could be paying 12% more.
How did your brain miss it?
Last year, Milke in Germany went from 100g to 90g. Same wrapper.
Only one tiny number changed. It's called shrinkflation.
It works because of how you shop.
Raise a price 1% and sales drop about 1.2%.
Shrink the pack 1%. Only half that.
You watch the price. Almost nobody watches the grams.
So brands shrink. In US stores,
after a downsize, the price per unit rose about 12 percent.
In 2016, Toblerone widened the gaps between its peaks.
Fewer mountains, same price. In May, a German court said Milka
misled shoppers. That's the mirage. Prices don't only rise on the tag,
they rise inside the pack. So skip the big number,
